cells.1 Introduction!A1: SHEET 1 - INTRODUCTION : BEST POLYETHYLENE (PE) PCF CALCULATOR  V5.8
cells.1 Introduction!B8: Calculates the cradle-to-gate product carbon footprint of polyethylene (LDPE, HDPE, LLDPE). Complete this blank template with facility-specific activity data and traceable emission factors.
cells.1 Introduction!B14:
- Declared unit: 1 t specification-compliant PE resin (pellets / granules, unpackaged) at the factory gate.
- Result unit: t CO₂e per t PE (= kg CO₂e / kg), AR6 GWP-100.
- One workbook per route and grade; interpret the PCF with its breakdown, allocation, data quality (DQR, PDS), assumptions and calculation status.
cells.1 Introduction!B17: Read the Instructions sheet, complete the applicable input sheets, and resolve all blocking validation issues before reporting the result.
cells.1 Introduction!B20: ="Data mode: "&DataMode&"   ·   Calculation: "&calc_status&"   ·   Benchmark: "&bench_status&"   ·   Verification: "&verif_status&"   ·   PCF: "&IF(n_block>0,"blocked",TEXT(pcf,"0.000")&" tCO₂e/t")
cells.2 Instructions!B5: STEP 1 — DEFINE THE FACILITY AND PRODUCT: complete setup : facility, reporting year, route, catalyst / initiator system, ethylene and hydrogen supply basis, allocation basis, and the grade declaration (density, MFR, grade / end use, CoA). Density is informational and does not change the PCF.
cells.2 Instructions!B6:
STEP 2 — ENTER MATERIAL AND PRODUCTION DATA (Sheet 4):
(i) fresh ethylene, comonomer, hydrogen, diluent / solvent / ICA make-up and CTA; (ii) catalysts, initiators, co-catalysts, adsorbents (annualised — never cut off); (iii) additives and chemicals (cut-off < 1 % each); (iv) PE and co-products with disposition (sold / internal fuel / recycle) and, for economic allocation, prices; (v) internal recycle loops; (vi) flare, vent, fugitive CH₄ and refrigerant losses; (vii) wastes and wastewater with attribution.
Give carbon fractions where requested; blank = not reported, enter 0 only for a confirmed zero.
cells.2 Instructions!B7:
STEP 3 — ENTER ENERGY AND UTILITIES:
Record each fuel stream once in the fuel ledger. Enter its quantity, unit, required fuel properties, and end-use distribution. End-use shares must total 100%..Complete electricity supply and consumption, on-site generation, steam and heat flows, water, and industrial gases. Distinguish purchased utilities from internally generated or recovered supplies.

Provide evidence for any contractual electricity claims. Avoid counting the same fuel emissions again through internally generated electricity or steam
cells.2 Instructions!B8: STEP 4 — ENTER TRANSPORT DATA: inbound legs and waste haulage not already inside a cradle-to-gate factor. Check each factor boundary first; outbound distribution of PE is outside the boundary.
cells.2 Instructions!B9:
STEP 5 — COMPLETE WASTE AND CARBON CAPTURE DATA
Specify the treatment route and required characteristics for each waste or wastewater stream. Where carbon capture applies, provide the source, captured quantity, energy and material requirements, destination, permanence evidence, and claim ownership. Captured or sold CO₂ does not automatically qualify for a deduction.
cells.2 Instructions!B10:
STEP 6 — REVIEW FACTORS, ALLOCATION AND DATA QUALITY: check each used factor on Sheet 10 (col R shows the Factor ID used; its source, table/page, data year, geography, technology and GWP basis are held once on the hidden sheet "Factor Metadata"). Prefer verified supplier PCFs, especially for ethylene (≈ 80 % of the PCF). 

Several suppliers or pathways: calculate the quantity-weighted factor outside the workbook and enter it as the Override (Sheet 10 col M) with the calculation and evidence (col N) and its boundary (col Q). Allocation: mass by default, economic where the value ratio exceeds 5:1 (BEST PE Section 6.7). Then complete sheet "8a DQR Assessment": answer the yellow questions per emission source (Unknown is an answer; blank is not), confirm the Factor ID in col P, and answer the compatibility checks (section C).
cells.2 Instructions!B11:
STEP 7 — CHECK AND REVIEW THE RESULTS. Fix every BLOCK (data missing or inconsistent; result not usable). Replace every PROVISIONAL factor (value not confirmed). Explain every WARN. Three statuses are shown. Calculation: BLOCKED / PROVISIONAL / READY.
 
Benchmark eligibility: may the PCF be compared with BEST tiers. Independent verification: your declaration; the workbook cannot verify. READY means the checks passed, not that the PCF is verified. Review drivers, assumptions, exclusions, allocation evidence and DQR.

cells.3 Setup!D16: North America · China · Europe · Middle East/GCC · Other. Leave BLANK to use the Default values (every use is flagged). 'Other' = no library values: you must enter your own factors (with source) on Sheet 10, otherwise the result is blocked.
cells.3 Setup!D17: One polymerisation route per workbook (route- and grade-specific results, BEST PE Section 5.6). Drives which rows apply on Sheet 4. LDPE copolymers (EVA, EBA, acrylates) are outside the methodology scope. Bimodal loop + gas-phase plants (e.g. Borstar): select the route of the final reactor and disclose the configuration.
cells.3 Setup!D18: LDPE: organic peroxide and/or oxygen initiator. HDPE: Ziegler–Natta, chromium (Phillips) or metallocene. LLDPE: Ziegler–Natta or metallocene.

cells.3 Setup!D34: Mass (Eq 1a) is the default. Economic allocation SHALL be used where the value ratio between PE and a sold co-product exceeds 5:1 (enter prices on Sheet 4 Section 4.7, cols U–V); it is checked by register W17/W18.
cells.3 Setup!D36: A completeness declaration. 'Normal only' understates the footprint and fails the comparability screen.

cells.8 DQR Assessment!A1: SHEET 8a · DATA QUALITY ASSESSMENT — screening DQR of the factor actually used   [INPUT: yellow cells only]
cells.8 DQR Assessment!A2: One row per emission source. The workbook retrieves the factor actually used (its Factor ID, source, data year and geography) from the hidden sheet "Factor Metadata". You only answer factual questions (yellow): does the factor represent your technology, how were the activity data obtained, were they independently verified — and, for an override or own factor, its data year, geography and type. Then confirm the answers for the current Factor ID (col P). Scores follow BEST PE Section 8.3 Table 3: 1 = highest data quality … 5 = lowest; the overall DQR is emission-weighted (Eq. 15). The DQR never changes a factor or an emission, and it is not a statistical uncertainty.

cells.8 DQR Assessment!B76: D · How your answers are scored (rules and matrix kept once, on the hidden sheet Factor Metadata, columns AD–AK)
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C77: Time · Geography · Technology · Precision. Each is met (1) or not (0) from the source record and your answers. Score = BEST PE Table 3: 0 met → 5 · 1 → 4 · 2 → 3 · 3 → 2 · 4 → 2, or 1 when independently verified.
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C78: Met when the underlying data year of the factor is within 3 years of the reporting year (BEST PE: primary data not older than three years). Data year not stated in the source → not met; a projection (data year after the reporting year) → not met. Physical constants and GWP values are not time-dependent → met.
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C79: Met when the factor represents the plant country (Setup C7). Regional or global averages → not met. Overrides: Q5.
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C80: "Yes — same technology / route" → met. Partly, No or Unknown → not met.
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C81: Met when the activity data are measured or calculated from measurements for the full period AND the factor is site-specific, supplier-specific or a physical property. Database averages, defaults and proxies → not met.
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C82: Only "Yes — verification reference held" allows a score of 1 (Table 3 tier 1).
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C83: "Unknown" is an answer (conservative: criterion not met; assessment complete). A blank = "Assessment incomplete": scored as not met and excluded from the assessed coverage. Col P must show the current Factor ID; if the factor changes, the row says RECONFIRM.
cells.8 DQR Assessment!C84: Share of gross emissions whose activity data are measured for the period and whose factor is site- or supplier-specific and within 3 years. The estimated carbon residual is never primary data.

cells.Factor Metadata!AE36: BEST PE Section 8.3 states that TfS operationalises the DQR on a 1–5 scale. The TfS PCF Guideline (v2, Section 5.2.11.2, as reproduced in UEIL/ATIEL 2024 Table 3) scores five criteria (technological, geographical, temporal representativeness, completeness, reliability) on 1–3 and averages them. This workbook keeps the BEST 1–5 tiers (governing) and uses the TfS level-1 definitions only to judge whether an ISO criterion is met.

cells.Factor Metadata!AE37: Table 3 assigns a tier both by data type (TfS column) and by the number of ISO criteria met (ISO column). They can disagree: a recent national factor of the plant country meeting three criteria is tier 2 by criteria but tier 4 by data type. The workbook scores by the criteria (evidence-based) and shows the data-type tier alongside (col T) for review.
